cards.explanation: The answer is False. Paul asks, “…did God reject His people?” and the very next words are “Certainly not!” No wiggle room, no “well, let me think about it.” Then he adds, “God did not reject His people, whom He foreknew.” That's a man who knows his answer before he finishes the question.

The answer is Benjamin. Paul, who calls himself an apostle at the start of this letter (Romans 1:1), says, “I am an Israelite myself, a descendant of Abraham, from the tribe of Benjamin.” He didn't just say he was an Israelite. He brought the whole family tree with him, friends. If anybody has a right to talk about Israel, it's the man with the paperwork.

The answer is that Elijah says he is the only one left. Elijah, a prophet of Israel, says to God, “I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well…” He has just said that the prophets are killed and the altars are torn down. I think that's a lonely thing to say, friends. He's telling it to God, though, and that matters.

The answer is that they never bowed to the false god Baal. God's reply was, “I have reserved for Myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal.” Baal was a false god (1 Kings 18:21, 39). Elijah said he was the only one left, and God points to seven thousand. Elijah was off on his count, and God did the reserving.

The answer is a remnant. Paul says it plainly: “…at the present time there is a remnant chosen by grace.” A remnant is what's left over, like the seven thousand God reserved in Elijah's day. Same pattern, different time. And notice it's chosen, friends, not just lucky.

The answer is False. There's no partly in Paul's words. He says the remnant is “…chosen by grace,” and then, “…if it is by grace, then it is no longer by works.” He adds, “Otherwise, grace would no longer be grace.” Grace doesn't take on a co-signer.

The answer is True. Paul says, “What Israel was seeking, it failed to obtain, but the elect did.” So Israel went looking and came back without it. The elect are the ones who did obtain it. Paul has been working toward that contrast for a few verses now, friends.

The answer is elect. Paul says, “What Israel was seeking, it failed to obtain, but the elect did.” The elect are the ones God chose, the same people as the remnant chosen by grace. They got what the rest were seeking. Then Paul says, “The others were hardened…”

The answer is eyes that could not see and ears that could not hear. That's the phrase, word for word: “…eyes that could not see, and ears that could not hear, to this very day.” Seeing and hearing are exactly what's missing, friends. Paul says it's “…as it is written…” so he's pointing back to Scripture.
